senses.gloss: something glistening, foil. Tanḥ. Vayetsé 12 (describing the Teraphim) מביאין … וכותבין על צ׳ זהב וכ׳ they get a firstborn man and slaughter him …, and write the name of a spirit of uncleanness on a golden plate, and put the plate under his tongue with sorcerous ceremonies &c.—Esp. the highpriest’s front plate.
units: <cite ref="Sukkah 5a:11">Succ. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>צ׳ דומה כמין טס וכ׳</he> the front plate was something like a gold foil &c.; <cite ref="Shabbat 63b:15">Sabb. 63ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Zevachim 88b:8">Zeb. 88ᵇ</cite> <he>צ׳ … עזות פנים</he> the plate procures forgiveness for sins committed by effrontery.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71:5">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> <he>בזה צ׳ ובזה צ׳</he> in this (the tribe of Levi) is the sheen (of the high priest’s frontlet), and in that (the tribe of Judah) is the splendor (of the crown, <cite ref="Psalms 132:18">Ps. CXXXII, 18</cite>); a. fr.—[Pl. <he>צִיצִין</he>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 3:4">Tosef. Sot. III, 4</cite> ed. Zuck. <he>בצ׳</he> with fineries, v. <cite ref="R00541"><he>צִלְצוּל</he></cite>.]

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53:3">Gen. R. s. 53</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 40:8">Is. XL, 8</cite>) <he>יבש … ונבל צִיצוֹ</he> the flower of Abimelech was dried up, and his blossom faded (his procreative faculty was lost); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 309">Yalk. Is. 309</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="R00438"><he>צִיצִים</he></cite>, <he>צִיצִין</he>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 145b:15">Sabb. 145ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 27:6">Is. XXVII, 6</cite>) <he>אלו … עושין צ׳ וכ׳</he> this refers to the scholars in Babylonia who create blossoms and flowers for the Torah (revive learning); a. e.

senses.gloss: filament, thread, thread-like shred, fringe. Ib. 131ᵃ Ms. M., v. צוּץ.—Pl. as ab. Ib. 94ᵇ; Tosef. ib. IX (X), 12 צפורן … וצ׳ וכ׳ a nail, and shreds (of skin) the largest portions of which are severed from the body.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 19:6">Sabb. XIX, 6</cite> <he>צ׳ המעכבין וכ׳</he> shreds of the corona which make the circumcision invalid. Y. ib. XIX, 17ᵃ; a. fr.—

V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 6:2">VI</cite>), 2 (describing a scarab or dragon used as an emblem of idolatry, v. <cite ref="D01123"><he>דְּרָקוֹן</he></cite>) <he>כל שהצ׳ יוצאין מצוארו</he> from whose neck fringes come forth; Y. ib.
